summary: Implement the 6 Miri WLED usermods, one parallel worker per mod, each shipping its own PR off main

tasks.name: miri-core
tasks.scopedGoal: Implement the MiriCore WLED usermod exactly as specified in docs/miri-mods/miri-core.md (read that file first; it is authoritative). MiriCore is the integration layer for all Miri sub-mods: sub-mod registration order, Miri branding, alert management, an I2C bus broker (pin definitions only, NOT bus owner), and the miri-ui.js panel loader. Deliver the shared framework under usermods/miri/ that the other Miri mods consume: usermods/miri/miri_env.ini (PlatformIO bundle env named miri_esp32 bundling all Miri build flags), usermods/miri/miri_pins.h (abstract GPIO/I2C pin names, every define wrapped in #ifndef guards, including MIRI_I2C_SDA=21 / MIRI_I2C_SCL=22 and MIRI_LP_I2C_SDA/SCL and MIRI_PIN_ADC_FUSE), usermods/miri/miri_shared.h (a MiriState struct with at least tempCelsius, overTemp, voltageIn_mV, fuseBlown shared by sub-mods), the MiriCore usermod class (branding -> set serverDescription to "Miri", alert loop reading MiriState.overTemp and MiriState.fuseBlown on a configurable interval, sub-mod instantiation order Temp->Fuse->PWM->IICIe->ColorSphere, HTTP routes serving /miri-ui.js and /miri-brand.css, and a /miri/panel/[modname] fragment mechanism), and usermods/miri/data/ forked WLED web assets adding a #miri-panels div plus the miri-ui.js script tag where miri-ui.js fetches /miri/panel/[modname] fragments into #miri-panels. Use teal accent #2EB8B8 in web assets. Gate ALL Serial output behind #ifdef MIRI_DEBUG. MiriCore must own no hardware directly (broker/branding only). Preserve base WLED code; touch wled00 core minimally. Use the Miri-Pwm-CHhip-Dev branch and Miri_v1.0/usermod_v2_pca9632 ONLY as read reference (you may `git fetch` and inspect them) - never merge or branch from them; rewrite from scratch per spec. Your work must compile. Build with PlatformIO using the miri_esp32 env (e.g. `pio run -e miri_esp32`) and report the result; if the toolchain cannot be installed in your environment, still ensure the code is correct and complete and say so explicitly in your handoff Verification section.
tasks.brief: Authoritative spec: docs/miri-mods/miri-core.md and docs/miri-mods/README.md. Build flag: -D USERMOD_MIRI. Standalone: No (integration layer). WLED registers usermods via the usermod_v2 mechanism (see usermods/EXAMPLE/usermod_v2_example.cpp and existing usermods/*/usermods_list.cpp for the registration pattern in this repo). Sub-mods remain usable standalone with their own -D flags; miri_env.ini bundles them when USERMOD_MIRI is enabled.

Alert loop reads MiriState.overTemp and MiriState.fuseBlown with configurable interval
All Serial output gated behind #ifdef MIRI_DEBUG

tasks.name: temp-sensor
tasks.scopedGoal: Implement the MiriTempSensor WLED usermod exactly as specified in docs/miri-mods/temp-sensor.md (read it first; authoritative). Read the TI TMP1075NDRLR (U6) over I2C at address 0x49 on the main bus (SDA IO21 / SCL IO22), 12-bit temp register at 0x00 at 0.0625 C/LSB. Self-init I2C with Wire.begin(MIRI_I2C_SDA, MIRI_I2C_SCL) in setup. Write board temperature to WLED: emit "Board Temp" via addToJsonInfo() with an alert badge when over temperature, and serve a main-page drawer fragment at GET /miri/panel/tempsensor backed by live data from /json/info. Update MiriState.tempCelsius on each successful poll and MiriState.overTemp (true when temp > threshold, false when temp <= threshold - 2C hysteresis). Config keys: pollIntervalMs (default 2000) and overTempThreshold_C (default 70.0). The mod MUST compile and run STANDALONE with only -D USERMOD_MIRI_TEMP_SENSOR: when MiriCore is absent, define your own pin and MiriState fallbacks behind #ifndef guards (e.g. a local miri_pins.h / miri_shared.h shim) so you do not depend on the miri-core branch at build time. Probe 0x49 at boot with graceful degradation if there is no ACK. Gate all Serial behind #ifdef MIRI_DEBUG. Preserve base WLED code. Use Miri-Pwm-CHhip-Dev / Miri_v1.0 only as read reference, never merge/branch from them. Build with PlatformIO using a standalone env enabling USERMOD_MIRI_TEMP_SENSOR (e.g. via platformio_override) and report the result; if the toolchain cannot be installed, ensure correctness and say so in your Verification section.

tasks.name: fuse-monitor
tasks.scopedGoal: Implement the MiriFuseMonitor WLED usermod exactly as specified in docs/miri-mods/fuse-monitor.md (read it first; authoritative). Sample the input supply voltage through a 43k/1.5k divider on the ADC, compute VIN in mV using VIN_mV = VADC_mV * 29.67 (divider ratio 1.5/44.5 = 0.03371), detect a fuse blow, and write MiriState.voltageIn_mV and MiriState.fuseBlown each poll cycle. Use ADC_ATTEN_DB_2_5, esp_adc_cal_characterize(), and an 8-sample moving average; initialize the ADC after a 500ms boot delay. CRITICAL BLOCKER: the ADC pin MIRI_PIN_ADC_FUSE is GPIO0 PENDING hardware confirmation (boot-strapping pin + ADC2/Wi-Fi conflict) - DO NOT assume GPIO0 is final: make the pin configurable via miri_pins.h default, document the GPIO0 conflict clearly in code comments, and gate ADC2 reads appropriately if GPIO0 is used. Provide a main-page drawer at GET /miri/panel/fusemonitor showing a VIN bar and a fuse OK/BLOWN badge, debounce the fuse blow (N consecutive reads below threshold), and emit "Vin" and "Fuse" via addToJsonInfo(). Config keys: pollIntervalMs (default 500), fuseBlowThreshold_mV (default 1000), plus under/over voltage thresholds. Must compile and run STANDALONE with only -D USERMOD_MIRI_FUSE_MONITOR: when MiriCore is absent, provide #ifndef pin/MiriState fallbacks so you do not depend on the miri-core branch at build time. Gate all Serial behind #ifdef MIRI_DEBUG. Preserve base WLED code. Use Miri-Pwm-CHhip-Dev / Miri_v1.0 only as read reference, never merge/branch from them. Build with PlatformIO enabling USERMOD_MIRI_FUSE_MONITOR and report the result; if the toolchain cannot be installed, ensure correctness and say so in your Verification section.

acceptance: Compiles standalone with USERMOD_MIRI_FUSE_MONITOR

tasks.name: pwm
tasks.scopedGoal: Implement the MiriPWM WLED usermod exactly as specified in docs/miri-mods/pwm.md (read it first; authoritative). Control the Miri v1.0 LED outputs: four RGBW PWM channels driving MOSFET gates (LED_R=IO13, LED_G=IO12, LED_B=IO14, LED_W=IO27), two addressable strip channels via SN74HCS244 (Strip1 Data shares IO13 with LED_R - mutually exclusive; Strip2 Clock shares IO12 with LED_G; Strip2 Data shares IO14 with LED_B; Strip1 Clock=IO15), a CH_EN enable line (pin TBD) asserted HIGH on normal boot to enable U5 (SN74HCS244 OE#), and a PCA9633 I2C indicator driver at address 0x62 on IO21/22. Default LEDC: 1220 Hz, 12-bit - CHECK which LEDC channels WLED already reserves before assigning yours. On setup: Wire.begin + PCA9633 init (clear the SLEEP bit). Provide per-channel mode config (PWM vs strip) enforcing mutual exclusion on shared GPIOs. RGBW LEDC outputs must update on WLED state change. Integrate with the WLED bus manager for strip channels when strip mode is active. V1 has NO drawer; reserve (declare but leave unused) v2 config keys such as ch1ColorRole etc. PCA9633 I2C writes only on change. Keep loop() under ~1ms typical. Must compile and run STANDALONE with only -D USERMOD_MIRI_PWM: when MiriCore is absent provide #ifndef pin fallbacks so you do not depend on the miri-core branch at build time. Gate all Serial behind #ifdef MIRI_DEBUG. Preserve base WLED code. IMPORTANT: Miri-Pwm-CHhip-Dev (usermods/usermod_v2_pca9632_Bus/ and its wled00/bus_manager.cpp changes) and Miri_v1.0/usermod_v2_pca9632 are READ-ONLY references - you may git fetch and inspect them to port patterns, but you MUST rewrite on main and never merge or branch from them. Build with PlatformIO enabling USERMOD_MIRI_PWM and report the result; if the toolchain cannot be installed, ensure correctness and say so in your Verification section.

WLED uses LEDC channels for its own PWM buses (see wled00/bus_manager.cpp / wled00/bus_wrapper.h) - avoid collisions. Follow the usermod_v2 registration pattern.

tasks.name: iicie
tasks.scopedGoal: Implement the IICIe (Pixi2) daughter-board WLED usermod exactly as specified in docs/miri-mods/iicie.md (read it first; authoritative). Driver for the PCA9849PWJ 4-channel I2C multiplexer daughter board on the LP bus (Wire1): Wire1.begin(MIRI_LP_I2C_SDA, MIRI_LP_I2C_SCL, 100000). Channel select is via a 1-byte control register (bits B2:B1:B0). Support all 9 selectable board addresses in a board registry: 0x58, 0x59, 0x5B, 0x70, 0x71, 0x73, 0x74, 0x75, 0x77. The MiriBoard_IICIe driver should activate on address detection, perform channel select, and support a downstream scan. Provide HTTP routes per instance: GET /miri/panel/iicie/0x[addr], POST /miri/iicie/0x[addr]/channel, and POST /miri/iicie/0x[addr]/scan (manual scan ONLY - never scan automatically at boot). Provide an extensible user-peripheral template framework with documented copy-paste examples for AnalogPeripheral, DigitalPeripheral, and DisplayPeripheral, plus an auto-generated drawer built from the peripheral declarations. Must compile and run STANDALONE with only -D USERMOD_MIRI_BOARD_IICIE: when MiriCore is absent provide #ifndef pin fallbacks (MIRI_LP_I2C_SDA/SCL) so you do not depend on the miri-core branch at build time. Gate all Serial behind #ifdef MIRI_DEBUG. Preserve base WLED code. Use Miri-Pwm-CHhip-Dev / Miri_v1.0 only as read reference, never merge/branch from them. Build with PlatformIO enabling USERMOD_MIRI_BOARD_IICIE and report the result; if the toolchain cannot be installed, ensure correctness and say so in your Verification section.

tasks.name: color-sphere
tasks.scopedGoal: Implement the MiriColorSphere WLED usermod exactly as specified in docs/miri-mods/color-sphere.md (read it first; authoritative). This is a PURE WEB UI mod - no C++ color logic, no hardware, no MiriState dependency, and no Miri branding required. Provide a 3D color sphere picker that replaces WLED's native 2D color picker. Serve GET /sphere returning a PROGMEM byte array MIRI_SPHERE_HTML[] (place the embedded HTML in a header such as sphere_html.h) unless the asset exceeds ~40KB, in which case document and implement a LittleFS fallback instead. The sphere JS must POST color changes to WLED's /json/state in the form { "seg": [{ "id": 0, "col": [[R,G,B]] }] }. Modify the Miri web assets to replace the native 2D picker container at build time (NOT runtime DOM injection). Emit { "Color Sphere": ["/sphere", "url"] } via addToJsonInfo(). Optional config: a custom route path defaulting to /sphere. Start from the HTML prototypes in docs/miri-mods/color-sphere-assets/ - use 'sphere picker code index.html' (or an approved variant) as the basis for the embedded picker. Must compile STANDALONE with only -D USERMOD_MIRI_COLOR_SPHERE. Gate all Serial behind #ifdef MIRI_DEBUG. Preserve base WLED code. Build with PlatformIO enabling USERMOD_MIRI_COLOR_SPHERE and report the result; if the toolchain cannot be installed, ensure correctness and say so in your Verification section.
